subject: Discovery recap — Finly: p95 latency & streaming concurrency
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finly.com>, Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@finly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap — p95 latency, streaming UX, concurrency (Finly)

Hi Alex / Sarah,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the deep context on Finly's streaming use case. Quick recap from our call and the things we agreed to follow up on:

Pain points (what you called out):
- Intermittent p95 spikes for streaming responses (you mentioned 700–900ms observed on short prompts).
- Streaming UX: partial tokens arriving late / reflows on the client causing degraded user experience.
- Backpressure at high concurrency — you see sharp latency degradation above ~1.2k concurrent streaming sessions.

Current stack (as discussed):
- Frontend: web client + custom proxy for multiplexing streaming responses.
- Model hosting: self-hosted open models + some managed endpoints for burst capacity.
- Infra: a mix of on-prem GPU and AWS for burst; no unified caching/batching layer today.

Success criteria you mentioned:
- P95 target: ideally <250ms for short (<50 token) responses, or at least consistent under 400ms with graceful degradation.
- Smooth streaming UX with minimal token jitter and partial response stability.
- Predictable scaling to 1.5k concurrent streaming sessions with bounded p95.

Next steps (from Redwood):
1) Share discovery notes & screenshots (attached).
2) Schedule a 60-min technical deep dive with Aditya (SE) and Dev (solutions) to go over telemetry and trace examples.
3) Draft a mutual action plan for a short pilot focused on improving streaming UX and p95 predictability.

Attachments: discovery-notes-20260228.pdf, finly_latency_screenshots.png

If anything above is off, tell me — otherwise we'll grab a time next week for the technical deep dive.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
https://redwood.com

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finly.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@finly.com>
Date: Sun, 01 Mar 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — p95 latency, streaming UX, concurrency (Finly)

Thanks Marissa — this is spot on and helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

- Our observed p95 (short prompts) averages ~850ms on weekdays during peak; off-peak it drops to ~400ms. We are aiming for a consistent p95 <250ms across regions for the core search UX.
- Concurrency: baseline is ~1.2k active streaming sessions; spikes up to ~1.8k during peak events.
- Model: we primarily run a 13B open checkpoint with FP16 on our infra; sometimes burst to a managed service for higher capacity.
- Error profile: we get occasional 500s from our proxy when queueing/backpressure happens — about 0.2% of requests during peaks.

We'd like to see:
1) A technical plan for addressing prefix/KV cache and batching improvements for streaming.
2) Any latency profiles you have for similar customers (p95 by seq length & model).
3) Availability for a deep dive next week — prefer Tue/Wed mornings PT.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Engineering, Finly
alex.johnson@finly.com

Subject: Tech deep-dive checklist / telemetry we need

Hey Alex / Sarah — looking forward to the deep dive. A short checklist of the telemetry and artifacts that will let us make targeted recommendations:

- P95 latency broken down by region, model variant, and sequence length (bins: <50, 50–200, >200).
- Streaming token-rate statistics (tokens/sec) and per-connection bandwidth.
- Request size distribution (input tokens and expected output length).
- Current batching/worker config (batch size, batch wait, concurrency limits).
- KV cache hit rates (if using prefix caching) and typical prefix lengths.
- Error rates and 500s with timestamped examples and proxy logs for a couple of incidents.
- Any traces/spans linking frontend, proxy, and model backend for representative slow requests.

Also: are you open to a short pilot on our Dedicated or Private deployment for the pilot? That can give more predictable p95 under load — happy to discuss tradeoffs on the call.

I'll bring examples of tuning (kernel selection, continuous batching, streaming flush heuristics) and a rough timeline for a 2-week pilot.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
